question: Will "None of These Candidates" receive more votes than the winning margin in the 2026 Nevada gubernatorial election?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: NOTC typically 1.5-2% in NV governor races (2022: 14,866 votes vs 15,386 margin — narrow miss); in governor races it has rarely/never exceeded margin, but it often has in close Senate/presidential races (1998, 2016, 2022 Senate; 2016 Pres). 2026 Lombardo vs Aaron Ford polls within 2 pts either way; markets (Kalshi ~58% Ford, Polymarket ~60-66% Ford) imply ~D+1-3 margin. With margin SD ~4.5 pts, P(|margin| < ~1.3%) ≈ 15-21%. Independent Danielle Ford (~7% in one poll) may absorb protest votes, lowering NOTC share. No market on this exact question found.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off certified 2026 NV governor general results (per Wikipedia page): YES iff NOTC votes > (1st place votes - 2nd place votes). Election Nov 3, 2026.
- Event window: single election day Nov 3, 2026 (results certification after); as of 2026-10-22, 0% of the vote count elapsed (early voting underway).
- Ballot: Joe Lombardo (R, incumbent), Aaron Ford (D, AG), Danielle Ford (nonpartisan, State Board of Ed member), plus NOTC (fox5vegas, Oct 21 2026).
- Polls: Emerson Sept 5-8 2026: A. Ford 44, Lombardo 42, 11% undecided. Noble Predictive Sept 22-26 2026: Lombardo 42, A. Ford 40, D. Ford 7, 9% undecided. Politicalwire Oct 6: 'Lombardo barely leads'.
- Win markets (Kalshi, Polymarket) favor A. Ford modestly (roughly 58-66% range, mid-Oct 2026); no market on NOTC-vs-margin found.
- 2022 NV gov: Lombardo 497,377 (48.81%), Sisolak 481,991 (47.30%), margin 15,386; NOTC 14,866 (1.5%); Libertarian 14,919; independent Bridges 9,918 (Ballotpedia/Wikipedia). NOTC fell ~500 votes short.
- NOTC historically 1-4% in major races; peaks 4.70% (2002 gov), 4.54% (2012 Sen) (Wikipedia).
- Cases where NOTC exceeded margin: 1998 Senate (NOTC 8,125 vs margin 428); also (from memory, unverified this run) 2016 Senate, 2016 presidential, 2022 Senate. Governor races: none found exceeding margin since at least 2006.
- Total turnout likely ~1.0-1.1M; NOTC at 1.5% ≈ 15-16k votes, so margin must be under ~1.5 pts.
- A visible independent (D. Ford) may draw protest votes that otherwise go to NOTC; 3 named candidates vs 4 in 2022.
- Searched but not found: 2026 NOTC-specific polling; any October 2026 poll beyond those listed; 2018 governor NOTC exact figure.
calls.reference_class: Nevada statewide general elections (governor, Senate, president) 1998-2024 where NOTC was on ballot; governor-only subset

calls.reasoning: YES needs the winning margin to be under the 'None of These Candidates' (NOTC) share, which historically runs about 1.4-2% in Nevada governor races (2022 approx. 1.46%, recalled; 2018 approx. 1.9%). In 2022 NOTC (approx. 14.9k, recalled) fell just short of Lombardo's 15,386-vote margin. Polling for 2026 is a toss-up: Emerson in Sept had Ford +2; Noble in late Sept had Lombardo +2 with an independent (Danielle Ford) at 7%. Modelling the margin centred near 0 with a 4.5-5 point error gives P(|margin| < approx. 1.4%) of roughly 22-27%. The independent may take some of the NOTC protest vote. No market exists on this exact contract; the Kalshi party-winner market was not retrievable (429).

calls.reconciliation: Runs differed mainly in judgment: the SD of the margin (4.5 vs 5), the margin's center (0 vs D+1-3 per markets), and how much the Danielle Ford independent candidacy depresses NOTC. Factual figures (2022: margin 15,386, NOTC ~14,866; Sept polls) agree across runs; the 2022 NOTC figure was verified by Run 1 via Ballotpedia/Wikipedia. Senate precedents (2016, 2022) are from memory and unverified but do not change much. I take mean ~D+1, SD ~4.5, threshold ~1.3 pts given the independent on the ballot → ~0.21.
